name: IL-02
label: Safe D

key_factors: Donna Miller's large fundraising and outside-spending advantage
Republican nominee with no reported fundraising
Open seat after Robin Kelly's retirement, but no evidence of a competitive race
model.rationale: The district's D+18 lean, Miller's $2.4 million raised plus $4.5 million in outside support against a Republican with no reported fundraising, and Polymarket pricing the Democratic side at 97% all point to a safe Democratic hold. No polls or expert ratings contradict that picture.
model.watch: Any late polling showing the Republican nominee gaining traction, or a surge of Republican outside spending, would be the first sign this open seat is closer than expected.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Robin Kelly (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
This south Chicago-area seat is one of the most Democratic-leaning districts holding an open-seat election this cycle, with a partisan lean of D+18. Incumbent Robin Kelly is leaving to run for Senate, and Democrat Donna Miller enters the general election with a decisive financial edge: about $2.5 million raised and roughly $4.5 million in outside support, against essentially no reported fundraising or spending for Republican Michael Noack.

Prediction markets price the Democratic side at about 97%, and no expert raters flag the race as competitive. With no public polling available, the forecast rests on fundamentals, which strongly favor Democrats. The seat is expected to remain in Democratic hands by a wide margin.
